The bill is now before Senate Ways and Means. The documents give no bill text, so covered software, prohibited conduct, penalties and effective date are not stated.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, statewide cap on annual rent increases (barred from November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: Proposed statewide initiative that would have struck G.L. c. 40P, the statewide prohibition on rent control. In its place it would have capped any annual rent increase for covered dwelling units at the lower of the annual CPI increase or 5%. On June 23, 2026 the SJC (Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893) held that the petition relates to religion under art. 48 because it exempts facilities operated solely for religious purposes. The court remanded for a judgment declaring the petition noncompliant and enjoining its placement on the November 2026 ballot.
rules.key_value: Cap (proposed, never effective): lower of annual CPI increase or 5%

unverifiable_exemptions: dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law (G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. It must be held in a separate interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, beyond the reach of the lessor's creditors. Within 30 days the tenant must receive a receipt showing the bank name and location, the amount and the account number. The lessor must give a signed receipt when the deposit is received and a statement of condition within 10 days of the tenancy start or of receipt of the deposit, whichever is later. Interest of 5% per year, or the lesser amount the bank paid, is payable annually. The deposit or its balance must be returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax-escalation increases, and reasonable repair of tenant-caused damage beyond wear and tear, backed by a sworn itemized list. Deposit records must be kept for 2 years. On transfer of the property, the deposit passes to the successor in interest, who must notify the tenant within 45 days. Noncompliance forfeits the right to retain the deposit and carries treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees. Lease waivers are void. As amended effective August 1, 2025, EOHLC regulations may allow an optional fee in lieu of a deposit; the fee plus any deposit may not exceed 1 month's rent in total.
rules.key_value: Max deposit: first month's rent; return within 30 days; 5% annual interest (or lesser bank rate); treble damages for violations; fee in lieu of deposit plus deposit capped at 1 month's rent

rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront charges at or before tenancy start (G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or agent of the lessor may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than four items: first full month's rent; last full month's rent at the same rate; a security deposit of no more than the first month's rent; and the purchase and installation cost of a key and lock. Because this list is exclusive, landlord-charged application, screening and similar fees are not permitted (per the secondary source). After the tenancy begins, the lessor may not demand rent in advance beyond the current month or a deposit above the statutory limit. No interest or penalty for late rent may be charged until 30 days after the rent is due.
rules.key_value: Only first month, last month, deposit (≤ 1 month) and lock/key cost may be required upfront; no landlord application fee; no late-rent penalty until 30 days after due

rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the broker pays (G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD½)
rules.requirement: No person may engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless licensed as a broker or salesperson. A licensed broker or salesperson may contract solely with the prospective tenant or solely with the landlord or the landlord's agent. Any fee must be paid only by the party, lessor or tenant, who originally engaged and contracted with the broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Public assistance / housing subsidy (source of income) discrimination bar (G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
rules.requirement: It is an unlawful practice for any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against an individual because the individual receives federal, state or local public assistance (including medical assistance) or housing subsidies (including rental assistance or rental supplements), or because of any requirement of such a program. Landlords therefore may not reject or treat applicants or tenants differently because of voucher or assistance income or program requirements.
rules.key_value: No discrimination against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies (e.g. vouchers) or because of program requirements

rules.title: Fourteen-day notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease (G.L. c. 186, § 11)
rules.requirement: If rent due under a written lease is unpaid, the landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant defeats termination by paying or tendering all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the possession action. If nonpayment was caused by a government failure or delay in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days to notify the agency. The court must treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent, interest and costs are tendered within that time.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment; cure by answer date; at least a 7-day continuance for government payment delay

coverage.summary: Applies to tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.
coverage.other_conditions: Written leases only; nonpayment ground only.

rules.effective_date_note: No effective date in the text; current codified statute.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.
rules.review_note: This is a termination-notice rule, not a just-cause list. The documents show no statewide just-cause or relocation requirement in Massachusetts.

rules.title: Notice to determine a tenancy at will (G.L. c. 186, § 12)
rules.requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with three months' written notice. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than three months, notice equal to the payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, is enough. The notice may include an offer of a new tenancy on different terms. For nonpayment, the landlord may end the tenancy with 14 days' written notice to quit. A tenant who has not received a similar notice in the prior 12 months may prevent termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days of receiving the notice. Every nonpayment notice must contain the statutory right-to-cure notification. If it is omitted, the tenant's time to pay extends to the answer date, but the notice remains otherwise valid. The court must continue the hearing at least 7 days if nonpayment was caused by a government payment delay.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (or rental interval / 30 days if longer); 14-day notice for nonpayment; 10-day right to cure once per 12 months; at least a 7-day continuance for government payment delay

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants (G.L. c. 186, § 18)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for protected activity. Protected activity includes enforcing housing laws through judicial or administrative action, exercising rights under G.L. c. 164, § 124D, reporting code violations to the board of health or another authority or in writing to the landlord, organizing or joining a tenants' union, and paying rent to a unit owners' organization under G.L. c. 183A, § 6(c). Damages are at least 1 and at most 3 months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees. A notice of termination (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change in tenancy terms received within six months after protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal. The presumption is rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence of independent justification. Lease waivers are void.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal; damages 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, plus costs and attorney's fees

coverage.summary: Applies to tenants of residential premises; no unit-count, age or owner-occupancy limits stated.

rules.review_note: An anti-retaliation rule tied to termination notices; it does not list allowed eviction causes.

rules.title: State tenant-rights form must accompany a notice to quit for nonpayment (G.L. c. 186, § 31)
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given to a residential tenant must be accompanied by a form. The form must document any repayment agreements and give information on rental assistance programs (including RAFT), applicable trial court rules and orders on summary process, and federal or state eviction restrictions. It must prominently state that the notice to quit is not an eviction, that the tenant need not leave immediately, that the tenant is entitled to a legal proceeding, and that only a court order can force the tenant to leave. EOHLC develops and posts the form, with the clause (ii) information in the 5 most common languages besides English. No court, including the Boston Municipal Court, may accept a nonpayment summary process writ, summons or complaint for filing without proof the form was delivered.
rules.key_value: Form required with every nonpayment notice to quit; courts may not accept a filing without proof of delivery; information in the 5 most common languages plus English
